registration: node: pixel (i, j) is at x = xMin + i*cellSize, z = zMin + j*cellSize; row 0 = north (zMin)
encoding: rg16: elevation_m = (R*256 + G) * scale + offset; B = trust mask (0..255)
source: Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM, 1 m (bare-earth; coverage Lidar_Composite_Elevation_DTM_1m as served in November 2026), via the Defra Data Services Platform WCS (https://environment.data.gov.uk/spatialdata/lidar-composite-digital-terrain-model-dtm-1m/wcs)
attribution: Contains Environment Agency information © Environment Agency and/or database right 2026. Licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

raw.note: unedited DTM (2 m), same encoding; shows every earthwork and modern work as surveyed (composite of EA surveys)

residual.note: raw - natural (m), only inside mapped earthworks (0 elsewhere). labels PNG: (R*256+G) = `label` of the earthwork in `earthworks` (0 = none). Add a feature back at its date as natural + residual*mask(label).

boundsNote: Built for site.json origin 51.17888, -1.82619 and bounds x -2700..3700, z -2800..2200 plus a 300 m margin. If the origin or bounds change, re-run scripts/lidar/fetch.py stonehenge and scripts/lidar/build.py stonehenge.
notes: Engine grid = the NATURAL surface at 4 m: every mapped earthwork (barrows, the henge, Avenue, Cursus, Lesser Cursus, Durrington Walls, Woodhenge, Coneybury, Vespasian's Camp ...) and modern intrusion (A303 and A360 with cuttings and embankments, the old A344 line, car parks) smoothed out by masked interpolation, so no dated earthwork appears before its date. Earthworks come back through the Stonehenge landmarks (their own builders) or by adding `residual` per label. Not removed: unmapped earthworks (field systems / lynchets, small ploughed-out barrows absent from OpenStreetMap), plough-levelling itself, plantation drainage and military tracks narrower than the DTM can resolve; see research/lidar.md. Local datum = OD - 62 m, as site.json states (stones at about 39.9 m local).
